name: hinge-lid-fit

status.stage_4_manual_experiment: done for L1: a weak model (Hydrogen) solved seed 0 in 2 attempts (0.115 -> 1.0) with a full-edge chamfer -> L1 is the easy level; L2/L3 added
status.stage_5_mvp_code: in progress: tasks 1, 2, 2b, 2c done (245 tests); task 2d = small fixes P2/P3 + fast test subset

required_stack.framework: Harbor task: instruction.md, task.toml, environment/Dockerfile, tests/, solution/
required_stack.reward: one score 0..1 written to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, partial credit allowed
submission: at least one Harbor run log with its score

scenario.summary: Box with a lid on a rear hinge. Under each lid knuckle hangs a rib (lug). While opening, the rib hits the outer top edge of the rear wall at roughly 40-72 deg, so the lid cannot open to 110 deg.
scenario.symptom: the lid jams while opening, somewhere around 40-70 deg; closed position is fine
scenario.root_cause: the rear wall's outer top edge lies inside the circle swept by the knuckle rib around the hinge axis
scenario.design_decision_task2: lid prints top face down, so knuckles sit below the lid top and the axis is only ~0.5 mm above the wall top; the colliding material is a rib under each lid knuckle
decision_log: 0.4 stop window [110, 130] dropped: Claude Code showed it is geometrically unreachable with this rib (latest possible contact 56-105 deg, larger chamfers give no contact at all)
0.5 precision comes from two sides instead: clearance >= 0.3 mm while opening (enough must be cut) and a tight minimal-change score (over-cutting costs points)
0.5 clearance is required only from 10 deg: at 0 deg the lid rests on the wall tops by design (seal), lift-off gap is >= 0.47 mm at 10 deg on all seeds
0.6 go/no-go on the 0.5 design: Hydrogen fixed seed 0 in two attempts (2 parameters + precise test_fit feedback = guided search). Kept as level L1.
0.6 the true better fix is LOCAL: relieve the wall only where each rib passes (3 segments, ~25 of 85.5 mm), ~3x less material than a full-edge chamfer.
0.6 S3 thresholds are not shown as numbers any more (they leaked V_best); the agent gets the rule only.
0.7 task 2c results (30 level/seed cases x 7 variants): reference 1.0 and original 0 everywhere; full-edge chamfer 0.4 on all L2/L3; reliefs only as long as the rib 0; no false collisions.
0.7 accepted P1: L1/L2 have 2-3 identical ribs (count depends on box width), not always 3.
0.7 accepted P2: L1 S3 loosened to 5x/10x so a full-edge chamfer always gets full points.
0.7 accepted P3: L3 draw constrained so identical reliefs need >= 1.4x V_ref (reward <= ~0.82); in 2c they only cost 1.16-1.39x (reward 0.83-0.99).
0.7 kept P4: reliefs exactly as long as the rib score 0 (still colliding at the rib ends), no partial credit.
0.7 fairness: printability ignores features smaller than 0.2 mm (slivers from typing rounded world coordinates on L3 must not count as overhangs or thin walls).

enclosure.role: printed box with rear wall, top edge carries the seal band

lid.role: printed lid with hinge knuckles, a structural rib (lug) under each knuckle, and a module frame on its underside

hinge_pin.role: defines the rotation axis; cannot move

lid_module.role: e.g. display or LED board mounted under the lid near the rear edge; moves with the lid

interfaces_frozen: hinge pin holes: diameter, position and axis on both parts

seal_band.where: closed position, all around the top edge of the walls

expected_good_fix: L1: smallest asymmetric relief of the rear wall outer top edge. L2/L3: one local relief per rib (only where the rib passes, extended >= 0.3 mm beyond each rib end along x), each sized to keep >= 0.3 mm clearance over 10-110 deg, seal margin >= 0.3, wall >= 1.2
expected_bad_fixes: cutting the lid or its rib: breaks keep-in -> 0
symmetric 45 deg chamfer: eats the seal band (9/10 seeds in task 2) -> 0
chamfer by eye, too small: still collides or rubs (< 0.3 mm) -> partial credit only
generous cut "to be safe": passes S1 but loses minimal-change points; deep enough cuts hit the knuckle brackets -> 0
moving the hinge: forbidden, frozen interface
L2/L3: one full-edge chamfer: works but ~3x the reference volume -> 0.4
L3: identical reliefs sized for the largest rib -> visible S3 loss
reliefs exactly as long as the rib: rib ends rub (< 0.3 mm along x) -> S1 fails

spec.principle: Agent sees every measured requirement with its threshold; it is never told the cause or the fix.

gate.G1_valid_solids: both editable parts are valid closed solids (OpenCascade check)
gate.G2_hinge_interface: pin holes keep diameter, position and axis; pin does not collide with knuckles; clearance around pin within band so the lid can rotate
gate.G3_keep_in_keep_out: lid knuckles, knuckle ribs, enclosure knuckle brackets, module frame and seal band filled >= 99%; module volume empty
gate.G4_closed_position: at 0 deg no collision between lid (with module) and enclosure
gate.G5_seal: at 0 deg contact between lid and wall tops >= 1.5 mm wide all around (contact region eroded by 0.75 mm still forms a closed ring)
gate.G6_not_rebuilt: outer envelope within tolerance; volume of each part changed by <= 15%

score.S1_opening: rotate lid (with module) about the pin axis 0..110 deg in 1 deg steps: no overlap (> 1e-3 mm3) at any step from 0 deg, touching allowed; min clearance lid(+module) vs enclosure >= 0.3 mm at every step from 10 to 110 deg (pin excluded: its bores have 0.125 mm radial clearance by design). Progress (for partial credit) = 0.5 * angle progress + 0.5 * clearance progress; angle progress = (largest angle up to which both rules hold - original) / (110 - original); clearance progress = clip(min clearance over 10..110 deg / 0.3, 0, 1), 0 if any overlap.
score.S2_printability: thinnest wall >= 1.2 mm; no new overhangs steeper than 45 deg in print orientation (enclosure on its floor, lid top face down); features smaller than 0.2 mm (rounding slivers) are ignored
score.S3_minimal_change: changed volume (added + removed) vs the original, compared with the reference fix of this task (V_ref, found by the generator: the smallest valid relief per rib from an exact 2D scan, with the required length along x). Thresholds per level (see levels). The agent is told the RULE only: "full points if your change is within <factor> of the best known fix for this task, zero at <factor>", never the volumes or percentages.

reward.S1_not_met: 0.25 * progress (so any working fix beats any broken one)
properties: over-cutting is clearly visible: S3 carries 0.6 of the reward
cutting the lid, its ribs, the seal band or the brackets -> 0 (gate)

agent_gets: bug report: the lid jams while opening and cannot reach 110 deg
full spec with thresholds, zones with coordinates, frozen hinge, print orientations
minimal-change RULE relative to the best known fix (factors per level), no volumes or percentages
tools to check every requirement itself

agent_interface.variant: B: agent gets solids (B-rep) and CAD tools, never runs its own CAD code
edit_operations: chamfer(edge, d1, d2) incl. asymmetric (whole edge)
extrude_cut(plane origin, plane normal, plane x-direction, 2D polygon, depth range): sketch on a plane + cut, the generic way to make a local relief
query_tools: one run_check(id) per validation in the spec
test_fit = all checks, small reward cost instead of a hard budget
agent_interface.topological_naming: edge/face ids change after every edit: each edit returns the new described list; geometric queries do not depend on ids
agent_interface.tool_call_cap: high safety cap (~150), not a source of difficulty

architecture.principle: framework (cadfix) knows nothing about hinges; scenarios compose generic validations through data. Framework grows only by what the current scenario needs, in generic form.

concepts.Part: name, B-rep solid, editable flag, print orientation
concepts.Assembly: parts + joints (fixed, revolute with axis and range; prismatic later)
concepts.Zone: named keep-in / keep-out region attached to a part, moves with it
concepts.Check: evaluate(ctx) -> passed, score 0..1, metrics, details; registered by type name, declared in scenario data
concepts.Scenario: generate(seed) -> assembly + check spec + reward policy + bug report; own reference_solver
concepts.Operation: generic edit ops on any editable part; scenario may enable a subset
concepts.RewardPolicy: data-driven: gate checks, objective check with progress, weighted score checks

architecture.key_property: agent check tools are generated from the scenario spec, so every requirement is checkable by the agent by construction
architecture.geometry: edits on B-rep (OpenCascade via CadQuery); checks on meshes (manifold3d), regenerated after each edit; sweeps need fast collision

layout.cadfix/checks: collision.py, sweep.py, zones.py, contact.py, printability.py, change.py, interface.py
layout.cadfix/env: env.py (state, log, snapshots), server.py (MCP from registries)
layout.tests: unit tests per check, exploit suites (generic + per scenario)

harbor_mapping.instruction.md: bug report + full spec, rendered from scenario spec
harbor_mapping.environment/Dockerfile: python + cadquery + manifold3d + package + public task files
harbor_mapping.tests/test.sh: own copy of grader + pristine parts -> /logs/verifier/reward.txt

architecture.secrets: none needed: grader compares against the original and the spec, both public

per_seed: hinge axis position (sets the needed chamfer size)
L3: per-rib depth/extent, world pose (yaw, tilt, offset)

difficulty_knobs.tight_window: narrow set of valid chamfers (small seal margin, rib close to the wall)
difficulty_knobs.rotated_assembly: hinge axis not parallel to world axes
difficulty_knobs.far_coordinates: assembly far from the origin (large numbers); measure, but not the main source of the gap

randomisation.feasibility_check: per rib: exact 2D scan of the relief profile (asymmetric triangle top x side, 0.05 mm steps) meeting S1 for that rib, seal margin >= 0.3, wall >= 1.2; relief length along x = rib length + 2 x (0.3 + 0.05). V_ref = sum over ribs. Also store the best full-edge chamfer volume (L1 behaviour) and the identical-reliefs volume (L3 trap). Empty set -> seed replaced by seed+1000*k, logged.
randomisation.experiment: plot agent score vs knob level next to the reference (difficulty curve for the demo)

build_order: 2 DONE hinge_lid generator, sweep, feasibility (first hit 41-72 deg, asymmetric chamfer needed)
2b DONE clearance sweep, feasibility range, S3 thresholds (V_best for full-edge chamfer)
2c DONE levels L1-L3, per-rib reliefs, extrude_cut, V_ref, reward 0.6, brief/evaluate per level, acceptance tables (docs/acceptance_2c.txt)
2d small fixes: P2, P3, regenerate L1/L3, fast test subset (slow marker)
3 go/no-go on L2 (now) and L3 (after 2d) with Hydrogen and a stronger model, ops JSON via evaluate --hide-score
4 checks + reward as generic modules (cadfix/checks); test per level: original 0, reference fix 1.0, wasteful-but-working ~0.4 on L2/L3, broken <= 0.25, seal/brackets/lid cut 0
7 Harbor packaging + first OpenCode run (required log)

L1_easy.geometry: 2-3 identical ribs (count depends on box width), assembly axis-aligned
L1_easy.S3: lenient: full points up to 5x the reference fix volume, zero at 10x (a full-edge chamfer always gets full points)
L1_easy.what it tests: finding the clash and sizing an asymmetric relief

L2_medium.S3: strict: full points up to 1.15x the reference fix, zero at 2x
L2_medium.what it tests: L1 + realising the fix should be local (one relief per rib, with >= 0.3 mm clearance at the rib ends along x)

L3_hard.geometry: three DIFFERENT ribs drawn per rib, constrained so that identical reliefs sized for the worst rib need >= 1.4x V_ref; whole assembly placed with a random world pose (yaw 15-40 deg, tilt 0-8 deg, offset 20-200 mm), so nothing is axis-aligned
L3_hard.what it tests: L2 + sizing each relief separately + working in a rotated frame

measured_2c.L3 sweep time: ~2 s (rotated geometry distance query), L1 ~0.15 s
measured_2c.L3 seed replacement: 6 of 10 seeds replaced (one rib not fixable)
